successCriteria.description: The AuditRecord entity interface is exported from the audit module's model file and its `action` property is typed as `AuditAction` imported from `src/shared/types/index.ts` (relative path, no extension).

The IAuditRepository interface exposes exactly three operations: create (accepting Omit<AuditRecord, 'id' | 'createdAt'>, returning Promise<AuditRecord>), findByEntity (accepting entityType + entityId, returning Promise<AuditRecord[]>), and findByUser (accepting performedBy, returning Promise<AuditRecord[]>).

AuditRepository.create persists a row via parameterized INSERT ... RETURNING * and returns a fully-populated AuditRecord whose id and createdAt are DB-generated (createdAt is a Date instance, not a raw string).
AuditRepository.findByEntity and findByUser return an empty array (not null, not undefined) when no matching rows exist.
All repository methods propagate database errors by rejecting the promise (no catch/swallow/transform) — verified by a test that mocks pool.query to reject and asserts rejects.toThrow.
The module barrel (index.ts) re-exports the AuditRecord type and the IAuditRepository interface + AuditRepository class, matching the existing module barrel pattern.

Unit tests at tests/unit/modules/audit/audit.repository.spec.ts cover: happy-path create (asserting returned entity shape and that pool.query was called with INSERT ... RETURNING and the correct parameterized args), happy-path findByEntity/findByUser (asserting mapped camelCase results), empty-array returns when no rows, and error propagation via mockRejectedValueOnce + rejects.toThrow.
The module compiles under `tsc --noEmit` (strict mode) and contains no `any` type annotations — the row mapper uses Record<string, unknown> with `as` casts, consistent with existing repositories.

constraints: All database access must go through the AuditRepository class — no inline SQL or direct pool.query calls outside the repository file (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository).
No `any` type anywhere in the audit module; use `unknown` with type guards or `as` casts (no-any, severity high).
All SQL must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, ...) — no string-interpolated user values into queries.

The AuditRecord entity shape is authoritative as specified in the task: a single `details: Record<string, unknown> | null` field; do NOT add old_values/new_values, performedAt, or updatedAt columns/fields from the conceptual audit_logs schema.

The audit module imports AuditAction from `../../shared/types/index` (relative path, no extension) and the pool from `../../shared/db/connection` — matching the established import style of existing modules.
Test files use the `.spec.ts` extension (established codebase convention across all existing repository specs), placed under tests/unit/modules/audit/.
The audit repository is the audit sink, not a subject — it must NOT itself write an audit record for its own create/find operations (no audit-of-audit).
outOfScope: AuditService / IAuditService interface and implementation — the reconciled architecture lists these as owned by the audit module, but this phase (Phase 6 per PLAN.md) covers only the model, repository, and barrel; the service layer is not part of this phase.
Database migrations / DDL for the audit_logs table — no Knex migration files are created in this phase; the repository assumes the table exists.
Fastify routes, controller, or any HTTP surface for audit — this phase is repository-only.
Integration tests against a real PostgreSQL instance — only mocked-pool unit tests are in scope.
Audit record retention/purge, time-range queries (performed_at filtering), or action-type filtering beyond the three specified repository operations.

entityInvariants.invariant: An AuditRecord is immutable once persisted — the repository exposes no update or delete operation; the only write path is create, which inserts a new row and never mutates an existing one.

The `action` value of every persisted AuditRecord must be a member of the AuditAction enum (CREATED, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, BALANCE_DEDUCTED, BALANCE_RESTORED) imported from shared-types; the repository does not accept or persist arbitrary action strings.

`id` and `createdAt` are always DB-generated and never supplied by the caller — create accepts Omit<AuditRecord, 'id' | 'createdAt'> and the returned record always carries both populated (createdAt as a Date).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects the promise with the underlying pg error (e.g. unique-constraint violation, connection failure) without catching or transforming it; never returns null on the create path.
Returns an empty array when no rows match; rejects with the underlying pg error on failure.
Returns an empty array when no rows match; rejects with the underlying pg error on failure.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The AuditRecord model file must import AuditAction from the shared-types barrel using the same relative-path style as the existing module models (e.g. leave-request.model.ts imports LeaveStatus from '../../shared/types/index').

The AuditRepository must follow the established repository structure: interface + implementing class co-located in one .repository.ts file, a private rowTo<Entity> mapper converting snake_case DB columns to camelCase entity fields with new Date(...) wrapping for date columns, parameterized SQL via pool.query, INSERT ... RETURNING * for create, and empty-array / null returns for not-found.

The audit module barrel must re-export the model type plus the repository interface and class in the same shape as existing module barrels (e.g. export { AuditRecord } from './audit.model'; export { IAuditRepository, AuditRepository } from './audit.repository';).

The audit repository must import the module-level `pool` singleton directly from '../../shared/db/connection' (no constructor injection), matching how employee.repository.ts and leave-request.repository.ts access the pool.

The unit test must mirror the existing repository spec structure: jest.mock the connection module as { pool: { query: jest.fn() } }, a makeRow helper returning snake_case rows, beforeEach that resets mocks and reinstantiates the repo, and happy-path / not-found / error-propagation cases — matching leave-request.repository.spec.ts.

integrationPoints.why: AuditAction enum is imported from the shared-types barrel; the audit module's only cross-module dependency is shared-types (per the reconciled dependency map: audit → shared-types).
The module-level pg.Pool singleton is imported by AuditRepository for all SQL execution; no other DB access path is permitted.

The LeaveRequestService will consume IAuditRepository.create to write audit records on every state-changing operation (GP-002); this phase establishes the repository contract that later phases depend on.
